title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in these notes Grothendieck studies the boundary stratification of M_{g,ν}. Strata are indexed by 'MD-graphs' (Mumford–Deligne graphs), i.e. stable dual graphs. These are connected graphs with a genus function γ: S → N and marked points I → S, satisfying the stability condition card I_β + card Ã_β ≥ 3 at genus-0 vertices. The previous page builds a new MD-graph G' from G by replacing each vertex α with a stable graph G(α). It redistributes the marked points and the half-edges at α among the vertices of G(α). G' 'se spécialise dans' G, meaning the stratum of G' lies in the closure of the stratum of G. To describe the relation G' → G cleanly, he opens a digression, §6 'Morphismes de généralisation de graphes'.

An ordinary graph is G = (S, Ã, σ_Ã, o_Ã: Ã → S). Here S is the set of vertices, Ã the set of oriented arcs (or half-edges), σ the reversal involution and o the origin map. To G one associates its fundamental groupoid Π1(G). Its objects are S. Its morphisms s → s' are the reduced ('simple') edge paths from s to s', which correspond to homotopy classes of paths in the topological realization |G|. In other words, Π1(G) is the free groupoid generated by the graph. Π1 is strictly functorial in graph morphisms f: G' → G (numbered (41)), sending vertices to vertices and arcs to arcs compatibly with σ and o.

The next page continues the argument. f is recovered from Π1(f), on objects and via the commutative square (43) Ã(G') → Fl(Π1(G')) → Fl(Π1(G)). So graph morphisms G' → G are identified with groupoid morphisms Π1(G') → Π1(G) that send arcs to arcs. He then enlarges the class to 'morphismes généralisés' (morphisms of generalization). These are presumably groupoid morphisms sending each arc to an arc or to an identity, which encodes edge contractions. Such morphisms are exactly the specialization relations between boundary strata, i.e. the morphisms of the category of stable graphs.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The claim that Π1 is strictly functorial is correct. The next-page claim that graph morphisms equal groupoid morphisms preserving arcs is also correct: Π1(G) is free on the graph, and distinct oriented arcs give distinct reduced paths of length 1. This needs σ to be fixed-point-free on Ã, i.e. legs/half-edges treated separately, which is implicit for an 'ordinary' graph.

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of a graph as the free groupoid on its oriented edges; morphisms are reduced edge paths, i.e. homotopy classes in the realization; strictly functorial in graph morphisms
ideas.modern_name: free groupoid / fundamental groupoid of a graph (Serre, Higgins)
ideas.where_published: Groupoid viewpoint pervasive in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this exact statement unsure

ideas.what: Graph morphisms identified with groupoid morphisms Π1(G') → Π1(G) mapping arcs to arcs; generalized morphisms (contractions/'morphismes de généralisation') defined by relaxing this condition, to encode specialization of MD-graphs (stable graphs)
ideas.modern_name: category of stable graphs with edge-contraction morphisms (dual graphs of boundary strata of \bar M_{g,n})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998); Kontsevich–Manin; later Abramovich–Caporaso–Payne, Chan–Galatius–Payne (tropical moduli)
ideas.where_published: Only in these unpublished notes, as far as known; Esquisse alludes to the 'structure à l'infini' of the Teichmüller tower without this formalism

missed.claim: Grothendieck formalizes the specialization (contraction) morphisms between stable dual graphs through morphisms of fundamental groupoids. Graph morphisms are groupoid maps preserving arcs, and generalized morphisms relax this. This is an early, independent framing of the category of stable graphs that later underlies modular operads and tropical M_{g,n}, phrased in groupoid language suited to his Teichmüller-tower/π1 programme.
missed.quote: Le groupoïde π1(G) dépend fonctoriellement (dans le sens le plus strict !) du graphe G. D'ailleurs, un morphisme de graphes (41) f : G' → G
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical priority point for the category of stable graphs. The groupoid formulation links naturally to the way boundary strata act on fundamental groupoids at tangential base points, as in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory. The mathematics itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The material is standard: the free groupoid of a graph, plus the setup for edge-contraction morphisms of stable graphs. The only interest is historical, as an early, groupoid-flavoured formalization of the stable-graph category by Grothendieck that predates the published modular-operad literature.
